counterfactual.change: Reduced bodies[1].vx from -47.877 to -5.0 (single field, same dt/steps/gravity). Lower relative speed avoids the faulty high-speed collision impulse and energy stays ~656 J within bound, proving failure is impact-speed dependent.

explanation: Between step 6 and 7 the two circles collide at high relative speed (~48 m/s). Correct elastic/inelastic collision should conserve momentum and not increase total energy beyond ~10% +5J. Instead momentum in x jumps from ~-48 Kg·m/s to ~-787 Kg·m/s and total energy jumps from ~1790 J to ~23888 J. Body 0 (16.9 kg, initially near rest) is accelerated to ~51 m/s while body 1 (1 kg) retains ~45 m/s, implying the impulse is applied with wrong effective mass / sign or repeatedly within the 24 substeps of step 7, injecting energy instead of redistributing it. Lowering impact speed removes the anomaly.
vision_note: Frames 4 to 6 show two blue circles drifting very slowly toward each other with only tiny displacement between steps. At frame 7 they just touch and appear to slightly overlap/interpenetrate, with no large separation or explosive motion. [disagreement: The picture shows a low-speed, gentle contact rather than the described ~48 m/s high-speed impact and post-collision speeds of ~51 m/s and ~45 m/s with a 13x energy jump; no dramatic recoil or ejection is visible between 6 and 7, and the color coding is blue/white rather than the described orange/red/grey/green.]
